name: Wispr Flow
description:
Wispr Flow brings your meetings into Claude.

Connect Wispr Flow to let Claude work directly with everything you capture — recorded meetings, transcripts, scratchpad notes, calendar events, and action items. No copy-pasting, no switching tabs. Just ask.

What you can do:

- Search and recall meetings — "What did we decide about pricing last week?" Claude finds the meeting, reads the transcript, and answers.
- Summarize and extract — Pull action items, decisions, and open questions from any recording or series of meetings.
- Stay on top of your calendar — Look up upcoming meetings, resolve calendar invites, and prep before you walk in.
- Capture and track tasks — Create, update, and search action items so follow-ups never slip.
- Work across your notes — Search and reference scratchpad notes alongside your meeting history.

How it works:

Once connected, Claude can query your Wispr Flow account in natural language — surfacing the right meeting, transcript, or note exactly when you need it. Everything stays tied to your account, accessed only when you ask.

Whether you're recapping a standup, prepping for a 1:1, or chasing down a decision from three weeks ago, Wispr Flow gives Claude the context to actually help.

Get started with Wispr Flow at wisprflow.ai.

protocolMetadata.instructions: Use this server when the user asks about meetings, notes, transcripts, or calendar information stored in Wispr Flow. For questions that may span multiple connected sources, use the relevant sources needed to answer the request. Read https://notes.wisprflow.ai/shared/ links with resolve_share_link rather than fetching the page. All timestamps returned by these tools are UTC (ISO 8601, ending in 'Z'). Before showing any time to the user, convert it to their local time zone — never present the raw UTC value.

tool.name: search_meetings
tool.title: Search meetings
tool.description: Search or list the user's meetings captured by Wispr Flow Meeting Recorder. Use when the user asks about their meetings, calls, standups, 1:1s, syncs, or anything discussed in a recorded conversation. Returns the most recently modified meetings when no query is given. For meetings on a particular day, pass since/until (when the meeting happened, half-open). Filter by who was there with attendee_emails (matched against the meeting's linked calendar event) — the precise way to answer 'my meetings with alex@acme.com'. Each result lists up to 5 attendees (more are summarized — call get_meeting for the full list), start/end times, and a has_transcript flag; when true, follow up with get_meeting and view_transcript={} and answer from the transcript rather than the lossy notes summary. folders lists the Wispr Flow folders the meeting is filed in that the user can see (their own and ones shared with them), as {id, name} sorted by name; null when it is in none. share_link is the meeting's notes page in Wispr Flow. Give it to the user whenever they ask for a link. Who else can open it depends on that meeting's sharing setting, and this server cannot read or change that setting. If the user wants to change who a link works for, tell them to open the Wispr Flow app, go to the Notetaker tab, click the menu to the right of the meeting, and click Share — that opens the sharing settings for that meeting. A meeting with no share_link has no notes page yet — say so rather than guessing a URL. Results are paginated, newest first. If the response's has_more is true there are more matches: call again with cursor set to the returned next_cursor (copied verbatim) to continue. When more remain, a 'more' field spells out how many and how to continue. To answer 'all'/'every'/'ever' questions, keep paging until has_more is false. Paging is capped at 1000 results per query; truncated=true means more matches exist beyond the cap — narrow the query. Every timestamp in the response is UTC (ISO 8601, ending in 'Z'). Convert times to the user's local time zone before presenting them — do not show the raw UTC time to the user.

tool.name: get_meeting
tool.title: Get meeting
tool.description: Get a bounded range of the markdown notes, the complete derived markdown summary, the complete attendee list without email addresses, and (when requested and available) a bounded range of the recorded transcript of a specific meeting. Use after search_meetings to answer anything about what was discussed, decided, the action items, or who-said-what. Returns start/end times for when the meeting happened. The raw Lexical notes JSON is intentionally omitted; use `content` for the paginated markdown note body and `summary` for the Flow Summary body, whose next-steps section holds the meeting's action items. Prefer view_transcript={} and synthesize your answer from the transcript itself: the notes are an auto-generated summary that can drop details, while the transcript is the verbatim source of truth. Omit view_transcript only when you've judged the notes alone are enough (e.g. a quick high-level recap). Transcript responses are character-bounded; when truncated, use the continuation offset in the marker to request the next range. Content is also character-bounded and returns its first range by default; use view_content with the continuation offset to read more. The summary is always returned in full. folders lists the Wispr Flow folders the meeting is filed in that the user can see (their own and ones shared with them), as {id, name} sorted by name; null when it is in none. share_link is the meeting's notes page in Wispr Flow. Give it to the user whenever they ask for a link. Who else can open it depends on that meeting's sharing setting, and this server cannot read or change that setting. If the user wants to change who a link works for, tell them to open the Wispr Flow app, go to the Notetaker tab, click the menu to the right of the meeting, and click Share — that opens the sharing settings for that meeting. A meeting with no share_link has no notes page yet — say so rather than guessing a URL. Every timestamp in the response is UTC (ISO 8601, ending in 'Z'). Convert times to the user's local time zone before presenting them — do not show the raw UTC time to the user.

tool.name: resolve_share_link
tool.title: Fetch shared meeting
tool.description: Get the transcript, notes, or summary of a Wispr Flow meeting from a share link (https://notes.wisprflow.ai/shared/… or its bare slug). Use this rather than fetching the page, which does not include the transcript. Returns the title, Flow Summary (whose next-steps section holds the meeting's action items), owner, and the caller's role. The owner also receives their user-authored My Notes. Pass view_transcript={} when the user wants the transcript: a bounded range is returned only when the caller owns the note or is an explicitly invited recipient AND the owner's organization shares transcripts. Domain/team access, anyone-with-link access, or a notes-only organization returns transcript=null plus a transcript_access explanation when requested. When truncated, use the continuation offset in the marker to request the next range. Errors if the link is not a share link or no shared note is accessible for it. Every timestamp in the response is UTC (ISO 8601, ending in 'Z'). Convert times to the user's local time zone before presenting them — do not show the raw UTC time to the user.

If the user wants to change who a link works for, tell them to open the Wispr Flow app, go to the Notetaker tab, click the menu to the right of the meeting, and click Share — that opens the sharing settings for that meeting. A meeting with no share_link has no notes page yet — say so rather than guessing a URL. Every timestamp in the response is UTC (ISO 8601, ending in 'Z'). Convert times to the user's local time zone before presenting them — do not show the raw UTC time to the user.

_published_faq.name: How do I add Wispr Flow to Claude, ChatGPT, or Cursor?

acceptedAnswer.text: Add Wispr Flow to Claude, ChatGPT, or Cursor by connecting its remote MCP URL in each client's MCP settings. In Claude, add a custom connector. In ChatGPT, add an MCP app. In Cursor, add an MCP server under Settings. The MCP URL is https://api.wisprflow.ai/connect/mcp. This server requires OAuth, so complete the login prompt after you connect.

_published_faq.name: Is Wispr Flow MCP ready for ChatGPT and Claude?

acceptedAnswer.text: As of October 6, 2026, Wispr Flow scores 96/100 on Manufact's MCP publishing checklist. The scan meets ChatGPT publishing checks and meets Claude publishing checks. Passing these checks does not guarantee marketplace approval.

_published_faq.name: How clear is Wispr Flow's MCP tool documentation?

acceptedAnswer.text: As of October 6, 2026, Wispr Flow scores 82/100 in Manufact's review of tool titles, descriptions, input and output schemas, and behavior annotations. The review covers 14 of 14 discovered tools. The quality score measures documentation clarity; runtime behavior and marketplace readiness require separate checks.

_published_faq.name: What tools does the Wispr Flow MCP server provide?

acceptedAnswer.text: Wispr Flow lists 16 MCP tools, including add_task, get_account_info, get_calendar_event, get_meeting, get_meeting_by_calendar_id, get_scratchpad_note, get_task, get_upcoming_meeting, list_meeting_series, list_upcoming_meetings, resolve_calendar_link, and search_calendar_events.

acceptedAnswer.text: Wispr Flow requires authentication. Connect it in Claude, ChatGPT, or Cursor and complete the OAuth login prompt.
